title: Cut: reconstitution and handoffs, on a feature branch
situation: 0076 part 5 had every ledger read and appended in the worktree the agent works in, and the architect started this cut in a worktree. The operator, 2026-10-10: a cut needs a feature branch of its own and nothing more; worktrees are not the normal development workflow and add complexity and hygiene overhead, and agents already know how to branch.
decision: One cut. (1) A computed overview of each context, read first at every reconstitution. (2) The workflow ships as its self-explaining capabilities. (3) The ledger of cuts and work packages is held by the harness's own agent lifecycle events: the cratylus extension appends a work package's lifecycle as it happens, dispatched when its builder is dispatched, returned when the builder returns, approved when its assayers' verdicts return. Each event carries a transition id, so a repeat is refused; events are entries of their own, created exclusively and versioned with the branch they belong to. (4) A completion check is a narrow fallback, never a gate on commits in general: it reacts only to an enumerated list of commit-message patterns and is silent on every other commit. The list holds one pattern, a cut's completion, a conventional commit scoped to its cut, as feat(cut:<id>): <message>. On such a commit it reads the named cut's state as the ledger computes it; when the ledger does not show that cut complete, it answers in the commit's output with a warning and instructions for the agent that made the commit, and it never refuses the commit. It fires only when the lifecycle events were missed, so each firing is evidence of a gap in their capture. A pattern joins the list only by a later decision. (5) Every cut is built on a feature branch of its own, and that is all the workflow prescribes about branching: how the branch is made and worked is ordinary development the agents already know. The ledger and the concept journal are versioned with the branch, so each shows the state of the branch being read; a cut's entries, acceptances and decisions about it included, are made on its feature branch and land with its merge. (6) Typed handoffs, with example 19 first. (7) The architect as principal (0070). (8) Every agent's default tools (0068).
consequences: Replaces 0076; accepted with the cut started on its feature branch. The workflow prescribes no worktree anywhere.
